candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'Fear ye not, ye souls of the righteous, and be hopeful ye that have died in righteousness. And grieve not if your soul into Sheol has descended in grief, and that in your life your body fared not according to your goodness, but wait for the day of the judgement of sinners and for the day of cursing and chastisement' — comfort to the righteous dead. The verbal pattern of 'fear not, ye souls of the righteous' is preserved in Tewahedo funeral liturgy as the consolation-formula for the mourning family.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'When ye die the sinners speak over you: As we die, so die the righteous, and what benefit do they reap for their deeds?' — the cynical sinner's epitaph. Tewahedo apologetic tradition uses 102:5 as the canonical presentation of the no-resurrection-no-judgment cynicism that the Epistle's argument refutes — direct anticipation of the Sadducean / Pauline argument of 1 Cor 15.
